pf-term1-bf-t1w4-highest-house-number.title: Highest house number
pf-term1-bf-t1w4-highest-house-number.instructions: Each player rolls a six-sided die three times to create a three-digit house number between `111` and `666`. After each of the first two rolls, the human player chooses whether the result becomes the hundreds, tens or units digit; the last roll fills the remaining position. The computer follows the supplied strategy: on its first roll, `5` or `6` goes in the hundreds, `1` or `2` in the units, and `3` or `4` in the tens; on its second roll, `4`, `5` or `6` goes in the hundreds if available, otherwise use the tens if available. Compare the completed numbers and report the winner. For the optional `4`-, `8`- or `10`-sided-die extension, display and compare each place value position by position (use separators when a roll can be `10`). Keep everything in one Java source file.
hints: Break the task into small methods with clear responsibilities.
Validate user input before using it.
Keep the main program and all helper classes in one Java source file.

pf-term1-bf-t1w5-word-hut-game.title: Word Hut Game
pf-term1-bf-t1w5-word-hut-game.instructions: Play the Word Hut game against the computer. Both players start with the same word, represented by a mutable note. On each turn, draw a random letter. If it appears in the current player’s note, delete one occurrence. Otherwise, if it appears in the other player’s note, delete one occurrence from that note. If it appears in neither note, append it to the current player’s note. The first player whose note becomes empty wins. Use helper classes such as LetterBag, Note and Player, all declared in the same Java source file. Optional extension: count letters deleted from the player’s own note, letters deleted with the other player’s help, letters added, and draws absent from the current player’s own note.
